subject: grad
title: (R)GRAD.------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-3, second of two on book p245, paired with v2-p245-1. Continues Braxton's post-WW2 frame: 'the resulting affinity focus on (attraction to) creative black music that emerged in that same period must be viewed as not separate from the composite nature of European continuance.' (R)GRAD (the reality of gradualism) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality): the question is what gradualism produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with social-reality — the (R) prefix marking that real gradualism (the slow post-war absorption of black creativity) is what produced the European/Japanese receptivity. SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) and SOC-RT sit at the upper-center: SOC-RT-DY rises from the main line and carries RT-ALGN (reality alignment) on the upper-left. POL-P (political policies) branches from the main line to the right. INT (intention) rises from POL-P to the upper-right, and STF (source transfer) hangs from INT on the right margin. A vertical from POL-P runs down to MPT (manipulation) at the lower-center; INFO-INTR (information interpretation) hangs from MPT, and POL-SIGN (political significance) from INFO-INTR. The diagram exposes that real gradualism — not styled gradualism — produces intention and source-transfer as upper outputs and manipulation as lower output.
